subtitle: 20 Professional Prompts + Full n8n Automation Guide

includesNote: Includes: how I built ai-income-systems.com on Lovable using these exact prompts.

howToUse.heading: How to use these prompts
howToUse.intro: These are not templates — they are engineered systems. Each one has a role, a context layer, an output spec, and a format instruction. Here is how to get the most out of them.

items.title: Replace every [BRACKET]
items.text: Every bracket is a variable. The more specific you are, the better the output. “Online business course creator” beats “content creator” every time.

items.title: Start with Step 1 when there is a Perplexity step
items.text: Several prompts are two-stage: Perplexity for research, then Claude or ChatGPT for the deliverable. Do not skip the research step — it is what makes the output feel custom instead of generic.

items.title: Run it, then refine
items.text: These prompts get strong results on the first run. But the second run — after you tell the AI what you liked and what to adjust — is where the magic happens.

items.title: Use n8n to automate the repeatable ones
items.text: Prompts 16–20 are designed to be automated. Once you have run them manually a few times and you like the output, wire them into n8n so they run on a schedule.

items.title: Build the Lovable spec in Claude first
items.text: Prompt 07 is the secret weapon. Always write your Lovable spec in Claude before touching Lovable. That is exactly how ai-income-systems.com was built.

prompts.title: The Authority Content Architect
prompts.subtitle: Turns one core idea into a full 90-day content calendar across every platform.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a professional content strategist and publishing architect with 10 years building authority brands in online business and AI.

# CONTEXT
My business: [YOUR BUSINESS NAME AND NICHE]
Core audience: [DESCRIBE YOUR IDEAL CUSTOMER]
Main offer: [YOUR PRODUCT OR SERVICE]
Current platforms: [LIST PLATFORMS YOU PUBLISH ON]

# TASK
Build me a 90-day content system using this one core idea: [YOUR BIG IDEA]

# OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS
1. One “pillar” piece (long-form post, video script, or newsletter) per month — 3 total
2. Five derivative pieces per pillar, repurposed for each platform
3. Five short-form micro-hooks per pillar for social
4. The connecting narrative thread that makes all content feel like one brand story
5. A simple publishing sequence: what goes out when, and in what order

# FORMAT
Organise by month. Include specific titles, not placeholders. Make the hooks punchy — I need real copy I can use today.
prompts.produces: A complete 90-day content calendar with specific titles, hooks, and a cross-platform repurposing strategy: 3 pillar pieces, 15 derivatives, and 15 micro-hooks, all tied to a single narrative that builds authority and drives your offer.

prompts.title: The Newsletter Engine Starter
prompts.subtitle: Generates a full newsletter issue that reads like a human wrote it at 2am and nailed it.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a newsletter writer known for making AI and online business feel approachable, real, and useful — not corporate or hype-driven. Your tone is a smart friend who happens to know everything about this stuff.

# THIS WEEK'S ISSUE
Topic: [THIS WEEK'S TOPIC OR NEWS HOOK]
My take: [YOUR RAW OPINION — 2–3 SENTENCES IS FINE]
One thing I learned this week: [REAL THING FROM YOUR WEEK]
Current offer or CTA: [WHAT YOU WANT TO PROMOTE]

# OUTPUT STRUCTURE
- Subject line: 3 options (curiosity / direct benefit / controversial take)
- Opening hook: 2–3 sentences that make them read further
- Main section: insight or lesson, 400–600 words, conversational
- “This week's system”: one actionable thing they can do today
- Soft CTA that feels like a recommendation, not a pitch
- P.S. line that adds one more value nugget

# TONE RULES
- No “in today's fast-paced digital landscape”
- First person, casual, honest. Contractions always.
- Sound like someone who is actually doing this, not observing it.
prompts.produces: A complete, ready-to-send newsletter issue with 3 subject line options, full body copy, and a CTA that doesn't feel like a pitch. Plug in your raw inputs, get a polished issue in under 60 seconds.

prompts.title: The Research Synthesizer
prompts.subtitle: Uses Perplexity to turn any topic into a competitive intelligence brief in minutes.
prompts.body:
# USE IN: Perplexity (Pro mode recommended for deeper sources)
I need a competitive intelligence brief on: [YOUR TOPIC OR NICHE]

## MARKET LANDSCAPE
- Who are the 5–7 main players in this space?
- What are they charging, and how are they positioned?
- What do their audiences complain about most? (Check Reddit, reviews, forums.)

## CONTENT GAPS
- What questions are people asking that nobody answers well?
- What topics get search traffic but have weak coverage?

## POSITIONING OPPORTUNITY
- What angle is currently wide open?
- What would make someone the obvious choice in this niche right now?

## SOURCES
Cite all sources. I want real links, not summaries of summaries. Format the answer as a structured brief I can use as a strategy document.
prompts.produces: A cited, sourced competitive brief with real market data, pricing intel, content gaps, and a clear positioning opportunity. Run this before launching anything.

prompts.title: The Faceless Video Script Machine
prompts.subtitle: Generates a complete short-form video script optimised for retention and shares.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a short-form video scriptwriter for faceless educational channels with 100K+ subscribers. You hook fast, deliver dense value, and end with a reason to follow.

# VIDEO BRIEF
Platform: [YOUTUBE SHORTS / TIKTOK / INSTAGRAM REELS]
Topic: [YOUR TOPIC]
Target viewer: [WHO IS WATCHING]
Goal: [GROW FOLLOWERS / DRIVE TO LEAD MAGNET / SELL PRODUCT]
Target length: [30 / 45 / 60 SECONDS]

# SCRIPT STRUCTURE
- Hook (0–3 sec): pattern interrupt. No “hey guys, welcome back.”
- Problem agitation (3–10 sec): make them feel the pain or curiosity
- Value delivery (10–50 sec): useful content in punchy steps
- CTA (last 5 sec): one clear, friction-free action

# FORMAT
- Include on-screen text suggestions in [brackets]
- Mark timing for each section
- Write the voiceover as natural speech, not formal copy
- Give me 2 hook variations
prompts.produces: A production-ready video script with timing, on-screen text suggestions, 2 hook options, and a CTA. Designed for faceless content — no face required.

prompts.title: The Pinterest SEO Architect
prompts.subtitle: Generates an entire Pinterest keyword and pin strategy for organic traffic from zero.
prompts.body:
# STEP 1 — Run in Perplexity first
Research Pinterest keyword trends for: [YOUR NICHE]
Find: trending searches, seasonal patterns, long-tail opportunities, and which pin formats are performing right now.

# STEP 2 — Run in Claude with the Perplexity output
You are a Pinterest SEO strategist. I am starting from zero followers and need to drive organic traffic to my lead magnet within 60 days.

My niche: [YOUR NICHE]
My lead magnet: [TITLE AND WHAT IT OFFERS]
Landing page URL: [YOUR URL]
Research: [PASTE STEP 1 OUTPUT HERE]

Deliver:
1. 10 Pinterest board names, keyword-optimised rather than creative
2. 30 pin title templates I can customise
3. 5 pin description templates with a hashtag strategy
4. A 30-day posting cadence: pins per day and what types
5. The 3 pin formats driving the most link clicks right now
6. One “hero pin” concept for my first viral attempt
prompts.produces: A complete Pinterest traffic system: board strategy, 30 pin titles, description templates, and a 30-day posting plan designed to drive lead magnet downloads from day one with zero existing audience.

categories.name: Digital Product Creation
categories.blurb: Turn ideas and knowledge into sellable digital products.

prompts.title: The Digital Product Blueprint Generator
prompts.subtitle: Turns a topic idea into a fully structured, sellable digital product in one prompt.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a digital product strategist who has designed 50+ info products generating $1M+ combined. You know what sells, what people finish, and how to structure knowledge for results and minimal refunds.

# MY PRODUCT IDEA
Topic: [YOUR IDEA IN ONE SENTENCE]
Target buyer: [WHO BUYS THIS AND WHY]
Price point: [$X]
Format: [PDF / VIDEO COURSE / TEMPLATE PACK / ETC.]

# DELIVER
1. Product title — 3 options, clear transformation over clever wordplay
2. A one-sentence value proposition that hits the emotional outcome
3. A complete module outline with a description for each section
4. The “quick win”: what can they do within 30 minutes of starting?
5. A bonus idea that adds perceived value without extra production time
6. Sales page headline (3 options) and 10 bullet points
7. An honest risk assessment: what makes this hard to sell, and how to fix it

Be direct. If my idea is weak, say so and tell me how to fix it.
prompts.produces: A complete digital product blueprint: title options, full outline, quick-win structure, sales copy, and an honest critique. The difference between an idea and a product you can actually sell.

prompts.title: The Lovable App Spec Writer
prompts.subtitle: Generates a precise Lovable build prompt that actually works — no vague requests.
prompts.body:
# ABOUT THIS PROMPT
Two-stage prompt. Stage 1 runs in Claude to produce a Lovable-ready spec. Stage 2 is that spec, pasted directly into Lovable.

# STAGE 1 — Run in Claude
I am building a [TYPE OF APP OR SITE] using Lovable.
My app does: [CORE FUNCTION IN 2–3 SENTENCES]
Target user: [WHO USES IT]
Key pages needed: [LIST THEM]
Design vibe: [DARK/LIGHT, MINIMAL/BOLD, REFERENCE SITES]
Must-have features: [LIST CORE FEATURES]
Nice-to-have: [LIST OPTIONAL FEATURES]

Write a Lovable build prompt that:
- Specifies the exact page structure and navigation
- Describes UI components in enough detail for correct rendering
- Includes a colour palette (hex codes), typography, and spacing feel
- Lists all sections of each page in order, with content descriptions
- Calls out integrations needed (Stripe, email capture, and so on)
- Requests a mobile-responsive layout explicitly

Format the answer as a single clean prompt to paste directly into Lovable.
prompts.produces: A Lovable-ready build spec specific enough to get real results on the first try. This is exactly how ai-income-systems.com was built: Claude spec → Lovable → live site.

prompts.title: The Lead Magnet Converter
prompts.subtitle: Takes any knowledge you have and turns it into a lead magnet people actually want.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a conversion copywriter who specialises in lead magnets. You know the only ones that work solve a specific, immediate problem so well that getting the answer feels like cheating.

# MY KNOWLEDGE BASE
What I know or do well: [YOUR SKILLS, EXPERIENCE, OR KNOWLEDGE]
My audience's #1 frustration: [WHAT THEY STRUGGLE WITH MOST]
My email list leads to: [YOUR MAIN PRODUCT OR SERVICE]

# DELIVER
1. 5 lead magnet concepts: title, format, and what makes each irresistible
2. For your top pick: a full table of contents or outline
3. The opt-in page headline and subheadline
4. The confirmation email subject line and first 3 sentences
5. The one thing this must deliver in the first 2 minutes to justify every email I will ever send

# SELECTION CRITERIA
Rank the 5 concepts by speed to create, conversion potential, and relevance to my offer. Be brutally honest about which one I should actually build.
prompts.produces: 5 ranked lead magnet concepts with outlines, opt-in copy, and the first email — plus a clear recommendation on which one to build first.

prompts.title: The Pricing Architect
prompts.subtitle: Designs a tiered pricing strategy that maximises revenue without pricing people out.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a SaaS and digital product pricing strategist. You have helped bootstrapped creators design tiered offers that convert across budget levels and maximise lifetime value without devaluing the brand.

# MY OFFER
What I sell: [DESCRIBE YOUR PRODUCT OR SERVICE CATEGORY]
Current price (if any): [CURRENT PRICE OR “NEW”]
Competitor pricing: [PASTE RELEVANT PRICING DATA FROM PERPLEXITY]
My audience: [WHO BUYS AND THEIR BUDGET RANGE]
My costs: [WHAT IT COSTS YOU TO DELIVER]

# DELIVER
1. A 3-tier pricing structure with names, prices, and inclusions
2. The anchor strategy: what makes the middle tier the obvious choice?
3. One-time versus recurring: which model fits my offer better, and why?
4. The price I should NOT charge, and why (the dead zone)
5. A launch pricing strategy: start low and raise, or start at full price?
6. One upsell that adds real value without new product creation
prompts.produces: A complete pricing architecture with tier structure, anchor strategy, launch recommendation, and one ready-to-implement upsell — built for your specific offer and market.

prompts.title: The Sales Page Writer
prompts.subtitle: Long-form sales page copy that converts without sounding like a 2009 ClickBank product.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a direct response copywriter with 15 years writing sales pages. You write with honest persuasion: no fake scarcity, no hollow hype — just a clear articulation of who this is for, what they get, and why.

# PRODUCT INFO
Product name: [NAME]
Price: [PRICE]
What it is: [DESCRIPTION]
Who it is for: [IDEAL BUYER]
The #1 outcome: [MAIN TRANSFORMATION]
What they have tried before: [PAST FAILED SOLUTIONS]
Objections they will have: [LIST THE REAL OBJECTIONS]
Social proof: [TESTIMONIALS / RESULTS / YOUR OWN STORY]

# WRITE THE FULL PAGE
Include: headline, subheadline, hook story, problem section, solution intro, feature and benefit breakdown, who it is for and who it is not for, social proof, pricing reveal, FAQ (5 questions), guarantee, and final CTA.

# TONE
Confident, clear, honest. Reads like a real person, not a template.
prompts.produces: A complete, production-ready sales page — every section, every word — that you can drop straight into Lovable, Webflow, or any builder.

categories.name: Client Acquisition
categories.blurb: Find, pitch, and close clients without the awkward hustle.

prompts.title: The Cold Outreach Engine
prompts.subtitle: Generates personalised cold email sequences that get responses — not templates.
prompts.body:
# STEP 1 — Research the prospect in Perplexity
Research this company or person: [PROSPECT NAME + COMPANY]
Find: recent news, what they are known for, current industry challenges, their content and social presence, and any public pain points.

# STEP 2 — Write the sequence in ChatGPT
You are an outbound sales specialist who writes emails with 30%+ reply rates by being genuinely useful, not pitchy.

My service: [WHAT YOU DO]
My outcome for them: [WHAT RESULT I DELIVER]
Prospect research: [PASTE STEP 1 OUTPUT]

Write a 3-email sequence:
- Email 1: pure value or observation. No ask. Reference something specific.
- Email 2 (day 3): one case study plus one soft ask
- Email 3 (day 8): the honest breakup email that often gets the most replies

# RULES
- Subject lines under 6 words
- Email 1 under 75 words total
- No “I hope this email finds you well”
- One CTA maximum per email, never two
prompts.produces: A 3-email cold outreach sequence personalised to your actual prospect — not a generic template. Built to get replies, not just opens.

prompts.title: The Discovery Call Prep System
prompts.subtitle: Preps you so thoroughly you sound like you have worked with them for months.
prompts.body:
# STEP 1 — Research in Perplexity
Give me a full business intelligence brief on: [PROSPECT / COMPANY]
Include: business model, revenue signals, team size, tech stack, recent activity, competitors, and likely challenges.

# STEP 2 — Build the call framework in Claude
I have a discovery call with [PROSPECT] in [X] hours.
My service: [WHAT I DO]
Their business context: [PASTE PERPLEXITY OUTPUT]
My goal for this call: [BOOK PROJECT / CLOSE DEAL / QUALIFY]

Build me:
1. 5 diagnostic questions that show deep, non-generic knowledge
2. The most likely objections and exactly how to handle them
3. How to transition from discovery to proposal naturally
4. One pattern-interrupt observation that shows I did my homework
5. The close: how to end with a clear next step without being pushy
prompts.produces: A complete call prep brief: questions, objection handlers, a natural close, and an opening line that differentiates you from every other vendor they will talk to.

prompts.title: The Proposal Generator
prompts.subtitle: Writes a complete client proposal that positions you as the obvious choice.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a business development consultant who writes proposals that win. You know a proposal is not a list of services — it is a document that makes the client feel understood and certain.

# PROJECT DETAILS
Client: [CLIENT NAME]
Their stated problem: [WHAT THEY TOLD ME IN THE CALL]
Their real problem: [WHAT I THINK IS ACTUALLY GOING ON]
My proposed solution: [WHAT I WILL DO]
Timeline: [HOW LONG]
Investment: [PRICE + PAYMENT TERMS]

# WRITE THE PROPOSAL
1. Executive summary: what I heard, what I recommend, what the outcome is
2. Situation overview that shows I understand their world
3. Proposed approach: what I will do, in what order, and why
4. Timeline and milestones
5. Investment breakdown, framing value before price
6. Why me — specific, not generic
7. Next steps: one clear action to move forward

# TONE
Professional but warm. A peer conversation, not a pitch deck.
prompts.produces: A complete client proposal — every section — that you can drop into a document and send the same day. Designed to win, not just inform.

prompts.title: The Referral Activation Prompt
prompts.subtitle: Designs a referral system and writes the exact messages to activate it.
prompts.body:
# CONTEXT
My business: [WHAT YOU DO OR SELL]
Current clients or subscribers: [ROUGHLY HOW MANY]
Referral incentive I can offer: [WHAT IS REALISTIC FOR ME]
What the referred person gets: [THEIR BENEFIT]

# DELIVER
1. A referral system design: how it works, how it is tracked, what triggers payout
2. The email to existing clients and subscribers asking for referrals — conversational, grateful, not corporate
3. A follow-up for people who said they would refer but have not yet
4. A simple thank-you message for when a referral converts
5. Three ways to make referrals feel natural, not like an MLM

# CONSTRAINT
This has to work with fewer than 100 subscribers. No fancy software — just email and simple tracking.
prompts.produces: A complete referral system with email templates, a follow-up sequence, and a tracking method — built for small lists, no software required.

prompts.title: The AI Agency Positioning Brief
prompts.subtitle: Defines your AI service niche and the positioning that makes you the obvious expert.
prompts.body:
# CONTEXT
I want to offer AI automation services.
Industries I am considering: [LIST 3–5]
My background: [YOUR SKILLS]
Tools I know or am learning: [n8n, CHATGPT API, CLAUDE API, ETC.]

# PERPLEXITY RESEARCH (run first)
Research: what AI automation problems are small businesses in [YOUR INDUSTRIES] paying to solve right now?

# CLAUDE POSITIONING BUILD
Based on my background and this research: [PASTE PERPLEXITY OUTPUT]

Deliver:
1. My recommended niche: industry + problem + offer
2. My positioning statement — one sentence that makes my ideal client say “that's me”
3. Three services at three different price points
4. How to describe what I do without saying “AI automation” (too generic)
5. The first 5 businesses I should reach out to, and why
6. What I need to demonstrate before my first sales call
prompts.produces: A complete AI agency positioning strategy: your niche, services, pricing, and first 5 prospects — a blueprint for launching an agency that doesn't sound like everyone else.

prompts.title: The Email Sequence Architect
prompts.subtitle: Writes a 7-email nurture sequence that converts subscribers to buyers on autopilot.

You are an email marketing strategist who builds sequences that feel like conversations, not campaigns. The best converting emails would still be worth reading even if you never sold anything.

# SEQUENCE CONTEXT
Lead magnet they downloaded: [TITLE AND WHAT IT COVERS]

prompts.title: The n8n Workflow Designer
prompts.subtitle: Designs a complete n8n automation for any business process — node by node.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are an n8n automation specialist who designs workflows that work on the first run. You explain each node's purpose, not just its name, and flag common configuration pitfalls.

# WORKFLOW REQUEST
I want to automate: [DESCRIBE THE PROCESS IN PLAIN ENGLISH]

prompts.title: The Passive Income System Mapper

prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a digital business architect who helps people turn knowledge and skills into automated income streams. You are known for finding the minimum viable path — the fastest route to revenue before building complexity.

prompts.title: The Customer Journey Automator
prompts.subtitle: Designs the full automated customer experience from first click to repeat purchase.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a customer experience architect who designs automated journeys that feel human. The best automations feel like a smart team is watching and responding — not a drip sequence running on a timer.

# MY BUSINESS
What I sell: [YOUR PRODUCT OR SERVICE]
Price points: [LOW / MID / HIGH TICKET OFFERS]

prompts.title: The Monthly Revenue Review System
prompts.subtitle: Builds an AI-powered monthly business review that tells you exactly what to do next.
prompts.body:
# ROLE
You are a business analyst and growth advisor. I am giving you my raw monthly numbers and you are going to tell me what they mean and what I should do differently next month. Be direct — I need signal, not support.

# THIS MONTH'S DATA
Revenue: [TOTAL + BREAKDOWN BY PRODUCT OR SOURCE]
New leads and subscribers: [NUMBER AND SOURCE]
Email metrics: [OPEN RATE, CLICK RATE, UNSUBSCRIBES]
Traffic: [SESSIONS, TOP SOURCES, CONVERSION RATE]
Content published: [WHAT I PUT OUT AND WHERE]
Biggest win this month: [WHAT WORKED]
Biggest frustration: [WHAT DIDN'T]

# DELIVER
1. What the numbers actually tell me — not what I want to hear
2. The one metric I should obsess over next month, and why
3. What to stop doing, and why it is a distraction
4. What to do more of, with specific targets
5. One experiment to run, with a clear success metric
6. My 3 priorities for next month, in order
prompts.produces: A complete monthly business review: honest assessment, one metric to obsess over, what to stop, what to start, one experiment, and 3 priorities. Automate it in n8n: Schedule → input form → Claude API → email report.

automation.heading: How to wire these into n8n
automation.intro: n8n is free, open-source, and more powerful than Zapier. Here is how to connect it to these prompt systems so they run themselves.

steps.title: Install n8n — free, 5 minutes
steps.text: Go to n8n.io and start on the cloud free tier. You get 5 active workflows on the free plan, which is enough to start. For unlimited workflows, self-host on Railway or Render for roughly $5 per month.
steps.flow: n8n.io → Sign up free → New workflow

steps.title: Connect your AI tools via API credentials
steps.text: In n8n: Settings → Credentials → New → OpenAI (for ChatGPT) or Anthropic (for Claude). Paste your API key. Get your OpenAI key at platform.openai.com/api-keys and your Claude key at console.anthropic.com. Each run costs fractions of a cent.
steps.flow: Settings → Credentials → Add credential → OpenAI / Anthropic

steps.title: Build your first workflow: the weekly content generator
steps.text: Trigger: Schedule, every Monday at 7am. Node 1: a Set node with your business context. Node 2: an OpenAI node containing Prompt 01 with your variables pre-filled. Node 3: a Gmail node that sends the output to you. You get a full week of content ideas every Monday morning, automatically.
steps.flow: Schedule → Set variables → OpenAI → Email you

steps.title: Chain prompts for multi-step workflows
steps.text: A lead magnet download triggers a webhook, Claude generates a personalised welcome email, your email provider sends it, and the result is logged to a Google Sheet. The Claude API call costs roughly $0.01–$0.03 per email.
steps.flow: Webhook → Claude API → Format → Send email → Log to sheet

steps.title: Automate your monthly revenue review (Prompt 20)
steps.text: Set a monthly trigger for the 1st. Build a simple n8n form for your numbers. Run it through the Claude API with Prompt 20 as the system message and email the formatted report to yourself. Your monthly business review runs itself — you just fill in the numbers.
steps.flow: Monthly trigger → Form → Claude API → Email report

buildStory.heading: How I built ai-income-systems.com
buildStory.sub: No code. No developer. Here is exactly how Lovable and Claude became a live business.
buildStory.quote: I built ai-income-systems.com in Lovable using these prompts. The trick is using Claude to write the spec first — then feeding that spec to Lovable.
paragraphs: Lovable is an AI app builder that turns prompts into real, deployable web apps. Most people's first attempt looks rough because they prompt it like ChatGPT. The trick is using Claude to write the spec first, then feeding that spec to Lovable.

I used Prompt 07, The Lovable App Spec Writer, to generate a precise, structured build prompt that described every page, every section, the colour palette, the navigation, and the integrations. Then I dropped that into Lovable and had a working site in one session.

The whole thing — design, layout, content sections, Stripe integration plan, email capture — was built by describing what I wanted in plain English, having Claude formalise it into a Lovable-ready spec, and letting Lovable build it. Total lines of code I wrote: zero.

Every time I wanted to change something, I described the change to Claude first, got a precise Lovable prompt back, and pasted it in. The entire site was built in a single afternoon. Then it was live, on a real domain, taking real email signups.
